attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Foundry City Race 7K, Sunday 24 October 2027
Applicant: Foundry Lane Brewery Social Club
Issue: 3.3

Some background. Our committee has run this race for a number of years and takes the welfare of runners to heart. One of our longtime members is a retired paramedic who usually runs the race herself and is not on duty that day.

1. Event summary
A 7K race with 120 runners, starting at 08:30 in the Greenhill area of Port Halden. No ambulance will be stationed at the race; any ambulance would come through the 911 system.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 12 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Harbourside Medical Centre, 10 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Brook Street have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Every first aid post and cycle responder carries a radio on the medical channel, with phones as backup. All calls for an ambulance go through the medical lead, who gives the crew the access point and the nearest barrier to open.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Yuki Tanaka, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Foundry City Race 7K | Sunday 24 October 2027
Organiser: Foundry Lane Brewery Social Club
Race director: Samuel Adeyemi
Reference: RQ-41263

Overview
The Foundry City Race 7K is a 7K race of 7 km for 120 entrants, based in the Greenhill area of Port Halden. The start is at 08:30 and the course closes at 10:00.

Course
The course runs in order along Brook Street, Albion Road and Foundry Street, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Tram Street, Prince Street and Ferry Road. The finish is in Ferry Park lawn.

Course dimensions
Most of the course follows the older street grid. Measured building line to building line, Brook Street is about 5.5 m, Foundry Street about 4 m, and parked vehicles on Albion Road leave around 4 m. The field assembles on Brook Street over that width, and the finish chute is laid out in the same street, ahead of Ferry Park lawn.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Brook Street from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Foundry website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Foundry City Race 7K
Date: Sunday 24 October 2027
Applicant: Foundry Lane Brewery Social Club
Prepared by: Tessera Event Transport
Issue: 3.3

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Foundry City Race 7K, a 7K race in the Greenhill area of Port Halden with a 08:30 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Northline Barriers.
- Brook Street, Hatter Street to Dyer Street: closed 07:15 to 10:30
- Albion Road, Dyer Street to Hatter Street: closed 07:15 to 10:30
- Foundry Street, Garrison Street to Abbey Road: closed 07:15 to 10:30

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 07:15 until the last runner has passed.
- Tram Street at Albion Road: 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Prince Street at Foundry Street: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Ferry Road at Foundry Street: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Brook Street: traffic diverted via High Street and Queen's Road, signed from Hatter Street
- Albion Road: traffic diverted via Victoria Road and Regent Road, signed from Garrison Street
- Foundry Street: traffic diverted via High Street and Dock Road, signed from Garrison Street

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

6. Notification
Details of the event will be published on the organiser's website and shared through social media in the weeks leading up to race day.

7. Reopening
Roads will be reopened following the conclusion of the event, once barriers and equipment have been removed by the contractor.
